Market today: The mood is cautious, driven by rising 10-year Treasury yields hitting 2007 highs. This signals potential Fed rate hikes, which typically pressures growth-oriented tech and chip stocks, making your concentrated portfolio vulnerable.

Your holdings: SOXL (-60.03%) and SPAL (-37.18%) are leveraged ETFs showing significant losses and are flagged "SELL." Their stops are far from current prices, indicating a need for immediate review. SMH (-14.9%) is also a chip name flagged "TRIM" and is very close to its stop. Remember, margin amplifies these drops.

Watch: Keep a close eye on Treasury yields; continued increases will likely put more pressure on your tech/chip heavy book. Also, watch for any signs of stabilization in tech valuations.

Bottom line: Prioritize risk management on your leveraged and underperforming positions given the macro headwinds.
plays: Review SOXL (-60.03%) and SPAL (-37.18%) immediately. Both are leveraged, deeply negative, and flagged "SELL." Consider trimming or exiting to manage risk.
Respect the SMH stop at 540 (current price 541.54). It's a chip name flagged "TRIM" and very close to its stop.
Consider SOXS (inverse semiconductors) as a potential hedge against your chip exposure. Scanner entry 50.16-49.78, stop 48.95.
